key_insight: The paper introduces routing-aware pruning that removes two-qubit parametric gates when their expected fidelity benefit is lower than the cost of executing them on a given quantum architecture.
engineering_relevance: This provides a unified compilation rule for both NISQ and fault-tolerant systems, helping reduce circuit depth, gate count, and routing overhead while improving end-to-end fidelity.
method: Compare an architecture-independent lower bound for omitting a gate against hardware-specific execution cost.
Evaluate each two-qubit gate based on rotation angle, qubit distance, and noise level.
Use the pruning boundary to decide whether a gate should be kept or removed across NISQ and FTQC settings.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks show up to 48.6% fewer gates and up to 47.7% fidelity improvement in NISQ simulations, with FTQC analysis indicating pruning remains useful across multiple code distances and physical error rates.
watch_item: Pruning decisions depend on accurate hardware cost and noise models, so performance may degrade if calibration or routing estimates are inaccurate.
paper_title: Quantum Circuit Pruning: From NISQ Architectures to Fault-Tolerant Operations
